construct: Camurati-Engelmann disease is caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in TGFB1. Many variants disrupt latency-associated peptide interactions and increase active TGF-beta1 signaling; the disease mechanism is gain of function and produces progressive diaphyseal hyperostosis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Symmetric diaphyseal hyperostosis with bone pain, proximal weakness, waddling gait, and a heterozygous TGFB1 variant identifies Camurati-Engelmann disease; GeneReviews classifies its disease mechanism as gain of function.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Sclerostin loss, cathepsin K loss, ALPL deficiency, and RANK-pathway failure are real skeletal mechanisms but map to different high-bone-mass or mineralization disorders and not TGFB1-related progressive diaphyseal dysplasia.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The genotype and characteristic diaphyseal pattern converge on TGFB1 gain of function; no alternative matches both.
